title.narrative: Advancing Sustainable Water Access in Fiji’s Rural Islands with Solar Energy

description.narrative: The overall objective is to improve the resilience, sustainability, and affordability of water service delivery in Fiji's maritime islands. This is achieved by transitioning away from unreliable, fossil fuel-dependent water pumping systems to climate-resilient solar hybrid solutions. The project aims to reduce over 58,000 kg/CO2 per year in greenhouse gas emissions and generate annual operational cost savings of approximately AUD 56,000–75,000 for WAF. These savings will be reinvested to enable replacement of new assets and roll out similar solar initiatives in other rural water pumping locations, acting as a catalyst for wider uptake across Fiji. Ultimately, the project enhances the delivery of an essential basic service and supports Fiji's national goals for climate-resilient infrastructure.

This project, titled “Enhancing Resilience to Climate Change of Maritime Islands of Fiji, through solar hybrid powered water supply systems,” will transition water pumping from expensive, unreliable diesel generators to solar photovoltaic (PV) hybrid systems across seven sites. The project is a partnership between the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) and WAF, directly benefiting approximately 4,900 residents in Lakeba, Rotuma, and Vanuabalavu. Key activities include final technical design, procurement of resilient solar PV and battery energy storage systems (BESS), infrastructure installation, and comprehensive Operations and Maintenance (O&M) training for WAF staff and local operators. The diesel generators will remain as backup, ensuring resilience during major climate events.
